`crud.get_user_by_email(*, session, email) -> User | None` is defined at `backend/app/crud.py:34`. Application code calls it from 8 places. Every caller passes keyword arguments and treats the result as an optional `User`.

**`backend/app/crud.py`**
- `crud.py:46`: `authenticate` uses it to look up the user. If the result is `None`, it runs a dummy password hash to avoid timing leaks (`crud.py:47-50`).

**`backend/app/api/routes/users.py`**
- `users.py:61`, `create_user`: an existence check. If a user is found, it returns a 400.
- `users.py:90`, update own user: a uniqueness check. It returns a 409 if the email belongs to a different user (`existing_user.id != current_user.id`).
- `users.py:151`, `register_user`: an existence check. If a user is found, it returns a 400.
- `users.py:204`, admin update user: a uniqueness check. It returns a 409 if `existing_user.id != user_id`.

**`backend/app/api/routes/login.py`**
- `login.py:58`, `recover_password`: if a user exists, it sends the recovery email. It always returns the same response, to prevent email enumeration (`login.py:60-62`).
- `login.py:85`, reset password: it looks up the user from the email in the reset token. It returns a 400 if the user is missing, and it also checks `user.is_active` (`login.py:86-89`).
- `login.py:109`, `recover_password_html_content`: it returns a 404 if the user is missing. Otherwise it uses the user to build the email content.

**Impact of changing the signature**
- Five callers only test whether the result is truthy: `users.py:61`, `users.py:151`, `login.py:58`, `login.py:85` and `login.py:109`. Of these, `login.py:85` also reads `user.is_active`.
- Two callers also read `.id`: `users.py:90` and `users.py:204`.
- `crud.py:46` branches on `None` and passes the user on.
- If the return type changes, for example to raise instead of returning `None`, all eight call sites need updating.
- Test code also calls it. `backend/tests/utils/user.py:39` and several places in `backend/tests/api/routes/test_users.py` would need the same update.
